UX surfaceShared primitives every surface builds on — no direct UI.

Members

PHOTON_RING

Photon-sphere ring radius (× radius) — the bright thin ring.

DISC_INNER

Accretion disc inner/outer radii (× radius).

SWIRL_COUNT

Orbiting plasma particles inside the disc and their point size.

JET_LEN

Bipolar jet: half-length and base radius (× radius).

JET_TIP

Jet tip radius (× radius) — keeps the beam collimated.

JET_OPACITY

Jet opacity — a whisper, not a lightsaber. Sgr A*'s outflow is radio-faint optically; at chart scale the beams only hint the disc poles. Vertex fade multiplies it to nothing by mid-beam.

GLOW_SCALE

Warm glow sprite behind the hole (× radius) and its opacity — kept tight so the additive stack (disc + photon + jets + glow) doesn't wash the whole frame to cream at fly-in distance.

PHOTON_TUBE

Photon-ring torus tube thickness (× radius) and opacity.

DISC_OPACITY

Smooth accretion annulus opacity under the particle swirl.

DISC_SEGMENTS

Ring tessellation of the accretion annulus mesh.

DISC_LANE_FLOOR

Dust-lane math (disc node shader) — two detuned ring harmonics multiply into irregular dark absorption bands. LANE_FLOOR keeps the lanes translucent instead of cutting solid black; LANE_AMP is the modulation depth around it.

DISC_LANE_ANG_A

Lane harmonic frequencies — angular/radial for wave A and B.

DISC_CORE_EXP

Radial heat exponent — ISCO edge blinding, rim fading to dust.

DISC_A_FLOOR

Alpha envelope — floor keeps the outer dust faintly lit.

SWIRL_PUFF

Swirl vertical puff (× radius) and inner-thickness bias.

SWIRL_CORE_R

Swirl vertex ramp — near-white at the ISCO edge dimming to amber at the rim, which is what produces the glowing-ring silhouette.

SF_BELT

Small-body belts (asteroid + Kuiper) — the seeded Points annulus each kind: belt catalog entry renders. Radii live on the def itself (belt.inner/belt.outer); these tokens own particle size, opacity and the default vertical half-thickness fraction.

PX

Particle sprite size in px — small enough to read as rubble.

OPACITY

Overall belt opacity — translucent so orbits read through it.

PUFF

Default vertical half-thickness as a fraction of the annulus width when the def omits belt.puff — real belts are thin but not flat.

ALBEDO_JITTER

Per-particle brightness variation — vertex colors jitter ±this so the annulus reads as mixed albedos (dark C-types vs bright S-types) rather than a uniform dotted ring.

GAP_FREQ

Kirkwood-style gap frequency for the asteroid belt — the density modulation sin(r·GAP_FREQ) carves resonance lanes; the Kuiper belt passes a def-level 0 to keep its smooth classical disc.

GAP_DEPTH

Gap depth — fraction of particles rejected inside a lane (0–1).

SF_BELT_ROCK

Belt hero rocks — seeded irregular meshes riding each belt so the annulus reads as real varied debris (ice, metal, carbon, stone, dust; fragments through large bodies) instead of uniform glowing points. Sizes are fractions of the annulus width; every rock owns a Keplerian pivot (speed ∝ 1/√r) plus a tumble rate, both riding the shared satPivots update.

COUNT

Hero rocks per belt — fewer than before but each one is now a high-tessellation mesh: the annulus reads as a crowded debris field at fly-in distance without the vertex-memory blowup that 96 ultra-dense geometries would cost (~3M tris per belt).

DETAIL

Mesh tessellation — icosahedron detail for regular rocks and tetrahedron detail for fragments. detail is EDGE segments: icosahedron detail 24 → 20·25² = 12.5k tris/rock (~600k per belt) so silhouettes hold a continuous curve at fly-in zoom with no readable polygon edges; fragments stay coarser (sharp shard planes are their look — tetra detail 10 → 4·11² = 484 tris).

MID_FREQ

Mid/micro relief octaves — a single low-frequency noise pass makes every rock a smooth blob, so displacement stacks three octaves: the macro crumple (1×) sets the silhouette, MID_FREQ × adds the lumpy potato bumps real asteroids carry, and FINE_FREQ × grains the surface at regolith scale.

TEX_W

Class-texture canvas (px) — 512×256 equirect, 16× the pixel count of the original 128×64 strip so crater rims and mineral veins resolve as texture detail instead of smearing into noise.

TEX_GRAIN

Per-class feature counts, scaled to the hi-res canvas.

SIZE_MIN

Rock radius as a fraction of annulus width — fragments at MIN, regular bodies in the mid band, BIG_FRAC of rocks promoted to the large-body range (Ceres-class stand-ins, still far under planets). Kept small: a hero rock must read as a boulder drifting past, never as a planet-scale body crossing the frame.

BIG_FRAC

Large-body fraction + their size ceiling (× annulus width).

FRAGMENT_FRAC

Collision-fragment fraction — tetrahedral shards, smallest rocks.

JITTER

Vertex jitter — per-axis displacement fraction (0–1) applied to every vertex, so each rock is a unique irregular potato/shard instead of a sphere or a repeated cookie-cutter lump.

JITTER_FRAG

Fragments deform harder — broken shards, not rounded potatoes.

CLASS_STONE

Material-class mix — probabilities sum with the metal remainder to 1: ordinary stony (chondrite) dominates, carbonaceous + hydrated + dusty bodies next, then ice, and nickel-iron holds what remains. The class picks drive both the painted texture and the material response (metal glints, ice refracts).

(module scope)

(remainder → metal ≈ 0.16)

SPIN_MIN

Tumble rates in rad/s — fragments spin fastest (collision fragments do); asteroid rotations run minutes-to-hours.

SF_LOD

Detail level-of-detail — secondary geometry (atmosphere shells, ring discs, satellite companions) renders only while the camera is within PAD + size * SCALE of the body's anchor, so distant bodies draw as a single primitive like a streaming game world.

DEEP_REVEAL

Deep-tier reveal — while the camera sits inside the local bubble (this many chart units from the solar barycenter) black holes, external galaxies, dwarf galaxies and hierarchy shells do not draw at all: from the Sun's neighborhood the galactic centre is a radio point source, not a resolvable object. The volumetric Milky Way disc is exempt — it is the sky band the camera is embedded in. The value sits just past the neighborhood band edge (300 + 300) so one zoom tier out of home reveals the galactic hierarchy.

SOLAR_FAR

Solar-tier collapse — beyond this heliocentric camera distance the whole planetary diagram (±150 units to the Kuiper rim) subtends too little to resolve, so every solar body hides and the Sun swaps its photosphere for the same flat point glow the neighborhood stars wear: from Proxima's range (~1 060 units) the real solar system is a single bright star, never a resolved cluster. The threshold sits well clear of the belt so normal fly-throughs never trigger it.

SF_COMET

Comet rendering — a SF_KINDS.COMET body is a dark irregular nucleus wrapped in a sublimated gas/dust envelope (coma) trailing two tails. The ion tail is a long narrow streak pointing straight anti-sunward (the solar wind entrains plasma along field lines); the dust tail is shorter, wider and lags the radius vector because grains keep some orbital momentum — it tilts off the anti-sunward line and fans out. Both tails are PARTICLE STREAMS rooted at the nucleus — THREE.Points clouds of soft-glow grains, never quads — whose length and opacity scale with heliocentric proximity: sublimation scales steeply with solar flux, so the tail ignites at periapsis and dies on the outbound leg. Lengths are multiples of the nucleus radius (Halley ≈ 0.2 units → ~6.4-unit ion stream), so the proportions read correctly at chart scale where an honest ~10⁸-km tail would cross the whole map.

COMA_SCALE

Coma sprite diameter × nucleus radius — the sublimated envelope.

COMA_OPACITY

Coma opacity at periapsis — thins with the same factor as tails.

COMA_FLOOR

Coma brightness floor — an inactive nucleus still vents a faint background coma; only the tails fully die.

ION_LEN

Ion tail length as a multiple of the nucleus radius — the plasma stream reaches well past the coma before it disperses.

DUST_LEN

Dust tail — shorter, broader, lagging the radius vector.

DUST_TILT

Dust-tail lag angle (rad) — grains trail the comet's orbit, so the fan tilts off the anti-sunward line.

ACTIVE_FRAC

Periapsis window — fraction of the periapsis→apoapsis span inside which sublimation runs hard enough to grow tails. Solar flux falls as 1/r², so the thaw front collapses quickly on the outbound leg: active = clamp(((rMin + span·ACTIVE_FRAC) − r) / (span·ACTIVE_FRAC)) raised to GAMMA, and the tail clouds unmount (visible=false) below TAIL_OFF. Halley sublimates measurably out to ~3 AU against an 0.59–35 AU orbit → ~9% window; 0.3 reads correctly at chart scale where the tail should die before the orbit leaves the inner system.

PTS_CORE

Particle counts — each tail is TWO Points layers: PTS_CORE small bright grains forming the dense axial stream and PTS_HALO large dim grains forming the diffuse gas sheath around it. ~640 grains per comet ≈ a few draw calls total — far cheaper than the displaced-geometry alternatives and the only primitive whose silhouette can never render a hard edge.

PSZ_CORE

Grain sizes (× nucleus radius) — core grains are tight sparks, halo grains are big soft blobs whose overlap fakes the gas volume. Under additive blending each grain contributes a fraction of its footprint, so the grains run large: a sparse cloud of small sprites reads as confetti, not gas.

DUST_PSIZE

Dust grains ride slightly larger than ion plasma.

SPREAD_ION

Column spread — the half-width at the root (× radius) and the downstream fan factor: spread(d) = SPREAD·(1 + GROW·d) so the column opens as grains drift anti-sunward (solar-wind dispersion). Dust disperses far wider than the field-locked ion stream.

WID_FLOOR

WID_FLOOR keeps a residual spread when the tail shrinks toward apoapsis (the column thins but never pinches to a zero-width line).

SHEATH_W

Sheath layer — wider spread and lower opacity than the core it wraps (SHEATH_W × spread, OP_HALO × opacity); HALO_SLOW slows its grains (outer gas drags behind the entrained spine).

RATE_ION_LO

Emission rates — per-particle lifecycle d = frac(phase + t·rate) in cycles/scene-second. Ion plasma streams fast (magnetically entrained, ~5–20 s to cross), dust grains creep (~15–70 s). Each particle seeds a rate inside its layer's range so the stream never marches in lockstep.

DIM_LO

Per-grain brightness floor (DIM_LO) and lateral wobble — each grain rides a seeded sine sin(t·WOBF + phase)·WOB_AMP·spread·(0.25+0.75d) growing downstream (turbulence amplifies as the column thins); WOBF_LO/HI spread the wobble frequencies so the column shimmers instead of sloshing.

SZ_LO

Grain footprint — SZ_LO is the per-grain seeded size floor (sz[i] ∈ [SZ_LO, 1] × layer size), SZ_BASE + SZ_GROW·d swells a grain's quad as it drifts downstream — dispersing gas expands, so the column stays fused (overlapping soft blobs) all the way to the ragged tip instead of thinning into separated dots.

PTS_RAMP

Brightness envelope along a grain's life d — a smoothstep ramp over the first PTS_RAMP fraction (fresh grains glow in rather than pop), then (1−d)^PTS_FADE so every grain dies at its own distance: the tip dissolves grain-by-grain into a ragged comb. FADE stays shallow — a steep falloff starves the mid-tail and the stream reads as a stub behind the coma.

ZFLAT

Vertical flattening — the z spread is ZFLAT × the in-plane spread (the tail sheet is thinner than it is wide, like a real dust sheet seen edge-on).

GAIN

HDR grain gain — vertex colors are written as rgb·envelope·GAIN: values >1 push overlapping additive grains into saturation, which is what fuses a sparse cloud into a continuous glowing column — without it each grain stays a faint gray speck and the tail reads as confetti instead of gas.

WIND_K

Solar-wind gust coupling — grain brightness scales by 1 − WIND_K + WIND_K·windNorm so a storm visibly surges the stream (katsushika-style brightness waves down the tail).

SF_DETAIL

Photographic-surface tuning — the real-imagery rendering layer for planets and deep-sky objects. Photo masks feather a source image's rectangular edge into transparency so NASA/ESA stills composite into the black scene; MASK_PX caps the composite canvas (source images run 1–6k px but are viewed at tens of screen px). Ring UVs are remapped radially (RING_V samples the strip's center row) because RingGeometry ships planar UVs but the Saturn strip is radius-indexed. HALO_SCALE sizes the additive star-glow sprite against the body's drawn radius; CLOUD_*/EMISSIVE_* tune Earth's layered maps.

MASK_PX

Composite canvas edge cap (px) for masked photo textures.

MASK_INNER

Radial feather — the alpha ramp starts at this fraction of the half-extent and reaches zero at the corner, so the photo's square frame dissolves into space instead of showing a hard border. Under additive blending the mask is the ONLY edge control, so the inner two-fifths stays full-strength and the outer ~62% of every still is pure melt — galaxies and nebulae dissolve into the star field with no detectable rim.

MASK_LOBE_DIST

Nebula lobe-mask scatter — distance band, lobe radius band, and the per-lobe alpha range (base + jitter).

RING_V

V coordinate sampling the ring strip's center row (radius = U).

RING_INNER

Saturn ring radii as body-radius multiples (matches ring texture).

RING_STRIP_W

Procedural ring strip — ringed bodies without a photo texture (Uranus, Neptune) get a seeded banded strip painted at build time: RING_STRIP_* sizes the radius-indexed canvas, RING_BANDS seeds the tenuous ring count, RING_BAND_W/RING_ALPHA_* shape each narrow dusty band. Uranus's real system is 13 razor-thin dark rings; the painter biases thin + faint so it reads as a charcoal sketch, not Saturn's bright bands.

HALO_SCALE

Additive halo sprite diameter as a multiple of the star's radius — the eased tail (see _HALO_T* in procedural.ts) makes the outer third invisible, so 3.6 keeps the glow hugging the limb without ballooning into the bounded-ball look a wide linear ramp gives.

CORONA_SCALE

Corona sprite diameter as a multiple of the star's radius — the prominence layer hugs the limb (the wide atmospheric glow belongs to the halo sprite), so it stays well under HALO_SCALE.

HALO_OPACITY

Halo sprite opacity — kept under 1 so the limb stays crisp.

POINT_RADIUS

Galactic-star photosphere clamp (world units) — at honest chart distances every star beyond the solar tier is an unresolvable point of light: 0.003 u subtends under a degree even at the nearest fly-to standoff, so no marker can render as a planet-like ball adjacent to another body. The authored def.radius still sizes the luminosity halo, the pick proxy and the fly-to standoff — only the sphere, its corona and its satellites shrink to the point.

STAR_RIM_FALLOFF

Fresnel exponent on the luminous-sphere shader — how tightly the rim hugs the limb. ~2.2 keeps a bright core with a hot narrow bloom; satellites use the looser value so their small discs stay soft.

CLOUD_SCALE

Earth's cloud shell rides this multiple above the surface sphere.

EMISSIVE_INT

City-lights emissive on the night side — the map is black except lit land, so a moderate intensity glows only where the texture is.

NIGHT_LO

Night-lights dusk band — dot(worldNormal, sunDir) smoothstep edges gating the emissive node: fully dark below NIGHT_LO, fully lit above NIGHT_HI, so city lights fade in through twilight and never glow on the lit hemisphere.

ATMO_SCALE

Earth atmosphere rim shell — ATMO_SCALE lifts the fresnel shell just past the cloud deck, ATMO_POW tightens the limb falloff, ATMO_ALPHA the base opacity. DAY_*/DUSK_* are the dot(worldNormal, sunDir) smoothstep edges driving the day/dusk/ night tint migration across the terminator.

BUMP_SCALE

Terrain bump depth — the elevation map's grayscale gradient offsets the shading normal; at globe scale only a whisper of relief reads correctly (full-scale units would spike the limb into noise).

SPARKLE_FRAC

Fraction of the galaxy particle budget kept for sparkle points.

SPARKLE_PX

Sparkle point size (px) — slightly fatter than the dust field so foreground stars sparkle against the photo disc.

PICK_MIN

Minimum pickable radius (world units) — a body sphere smaller than this subtends only a few pixels at the home camera, so an invisible proxy bubble rides inside its mesh for raycasts.

PICK_PROXY

Pick-proxy radius multiplier — the invisible raycast sphere is PICK_PROXY × the body's true radius (never a fixed size), so honest stellar-scale bodies stay tappable without a fake giant bubble that would swallow neighbours at their real distances.

GALAXY_DISC

Photo-disc diameter as a multiple of the catalog radius.

SF_SPIKE

Diffraction-spike starburst — the telescope-optics cross that rides bright stars. Spikes are soft elliptical gradients (never stroked lines), seeded-rotated per star so no two crosses align. Kept as its own bag since the sprite is a separate layer from halo + corona.

SPIKE_SCALE

Spike sprite diameter as a multiple of the star's authored radius — like the halo it tracks luminosity, not the clamped point sphere, so catalog giants throw longer crosses than dwarfs. Sits a step beyond HALO_SCALE so the spike tips pierce the glow edge.

SPIKE_OPACITY

Sprite opacity — under HALO_OPACITY so it reads as optics, not gas.

SPIKE_RAYS

Spike ray count — 6 throws the hexagonal cross of a real segmented mirror (JWST), plus a faint second cross at SPIKE_ROT2 for depth.

SPIKE_ROT2

Second cross angular offset (radians fraction of a full turn).

SPIKE_LEN2

Second cross reach multiplier vs the primary rays.

SPIKE_THIN

Ray ellipse minor-axis width as a fraction of the half-sprite.

SPIKE_CORE

Center knot radius as a fraction of the half-sprite.

SPIKE_JITTER

Rotation jitter added to the seeded base angle (radians).

SF_NEBULA_DEPTH

Nebula depth layering — a parallax echo + wide underlay glow composed under the photo sprite so a nebula reads as a volume of gas at different depths instead of one flat billboard. The *_RATE/_FREQ/_WAVE members drive the ambient-life pass in updateFx: each layer swirls (SpriteMaterial.rotation is a UV-space turn, so the feathered photo churns in place rather than orbiting) and breathes opacity on detuned sines; rates are seeded from the body id so no two nebulae churn alike.

ECHO_SCALE

Echo layer scale multiplier over the photo sprite.

ECHO_OPACITY

Echo layer opacity — ghost of the photo rotated off-axis.

UNDER_SCALE

Underlay glow scale multiplier — the wide light-field behind.

UNDER_OPACITY

Underlay glow opacity.

SWIRL_MIN

Slowest layer swirl rate (rad/scene-second) — real nebular flows move at ~10 km/s over light-year spans, so the chart suggests the churn with sub-centi-radian rotation rather than a visible spin.

SWIRL_SPREAD

Seeded spread added to SWIRL_MIN — per-nebula swirl variance.

ECHO_RATE

Echo counter-rotation factor — negative sign makes the ghost layer shear against the photo.

UNDER_RATE

Underlay drift factor — the widest layer barely turns.

OP_WAVE

Opacity shimmer amplitude (fraction of opBase) + detuned frequency.

BREATHE_AMP

Whole-sprite breathing — ±fraction scale swell like gas pressure waves.
